subject: Staged rollup: narrow maintenance window + network drain / rollback process
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@quantigen.com>, ITChange <itchange@quantigen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged rollup: narrow maintenance window + network drain / rollback process

Hi Carlos / ITChange team —

We discussed a short maintenance window to apply the 2028-03 security backports and the recommended runtime pin (v1.14.3 -> v1.14.5) for your private VPC deployment. This thread is to lock the operational plan and confirm the narrow window + network drain approach so we can satisfy your change controls. Key points up front: 

- Proposed window: Friday 2028-03-10 02:00–02:30 PT (30 minutes).
- Scope: runtime patch, model-serving runtime bump to v1.14.5, LB connection drain, IP allowlist update (new egress CIDR), and healthcheck warmup.
- Canary: 5% traffic (single AZ) for first 10 minutes; then 100% if green.
- Rollback: instant pin back to v1.14.3 and revert routing to pre-window state; we must be able to complete rollback within 12 minutes.

Attachments: maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf (runbook + rollback steps), ip-allowlist-change-sheet.csv (new CIDRs), canary-warmup-checklist.md

Requests for Quantigen:
- Confirm the change window above or propose an alternate 30-minute window.
- Provide the firewall change ticket ID (we will update our side once you provide it).
- Approve the 5% canary in AZ-west-2 first.

Internal notes for Redwood ops: Ben / Dev / Lauren, please review the runbook attachment; Dev, can you validate the KV-cache compatibility across the two patch versions? We need a one-command pin rollback for managed hosts.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@quantigen.com>

Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged rollup: narrow maintenance window + network drain / rollback process

Thanks Naomi — quick notes:

- Agree with the 30-minute window. We will stage a green traffic shift plan: drain new connections at the LB, then wait 60s for inflight tokens to finish before starting the canary.
- Dev: confirm that the rollback command sequence in the runbook (section 4) includes KV cache flush and immediate kernel selector revert. I want this tested in staging today.
- We'll run the canary in the same AZ that hosts the warmup image to avoid cross-AZ cold starts.

Carlos — please tell us if you need any IPs added earlier than the 24h SLA on your firewall side. Otherwise we will proceed with the Friday slot.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@quantigen.com>

Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged rollup: narrow maintenance window + network drain / rollback process

Thanks Naomi / Ben — Quantigen Ops side:

- The proposed Friday 02:00–02:30 PT window is acceptable. Our CAB approved a narrow 30-minute window contingent on the IP allowlist changes being completed before the window opens.
- Firewall ticket created: QNT-CHG-3291. Expected rule apply: 2028-03-09 20:00 PT. Please confirm once Redwood has the final egress CIDR to whitelist; we can apply earlier if needed.
- A quick note on monitoring: we will watch CPU, token latency p95, and error_rate_5m. If any metric deviates >30% from baseline, we will trigger the rollback.

Two items from our side:
1) We cannot accept more than 2 concurrent connection disruptions. Please ensure the drain strategy keeps concurrency <= 2.
2) For rollback, we require a documented postmortem within 24h if rollback is invoked.

Carlos Ramirez
Head of Platform Engineering | Quantigen Health
c.ramirez@quantigen.com | +1 650-555-4332
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@quantigen.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged rollup: narrow maintenance window + network drain / rollback process

On Thu, Mar 8, 2028 at 09:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We discussed a short maintenance window to apply the 2028-03 security backports and the recommended runtime pin (v1.14.3 -> v1.14.5) for your private VPC deployment.

All — ops checklist and timeline (final):

T-4h:
- Confirm firewall ticket QNT-CHG-3291 shows "applied" (Quantigen ops).
- Redwood: run final preflight healthcheck (scripts in maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf).

T-30m:
- Push config to canary hosts (canary label: rollout/quantigen-20280310). Warmup containers follow canary-warmup-checklist.md.
- Update egress CIDR in Env (env var REDWOOD_EGRESS_CIDR) to the value in ip-allowlist-change-sheet.csv.

At 02:00 PT (start):
- LB: set canary weight 5%. Wait 10 minutes. Monitor token latency p95, CPU, and error_rate_5m.
- If stable: set weight -> 100% over 3 minutes (incremental). Confirm <30% delta.

Rollback (invoked if metric threshold breached or manual stop):
- Step 1: LB immediate reweight to previous stable pool.
- Step 2: run: /opt/redwood/bin/pin-runtime --version=1.14.3 --force (this reverts kernel selector and runtime path).
- Step 3: flush KV cache: /opt/redwood/bin/kv-flush --all; confirm hit-rate baseline.
- Step 4: revert env REDWOOD_EGRESS_CIDR to previous value.
- Postmortem: create JIRA INF-4521-rollback and deliver within 24h.

Testing notes: I ran the rollback command in staging and observed a 6 minute median completion time across 8 hosts (see runbook section 4.2). We will aim for 12 minutes upper bound in prod.

I will be on call 01:30–03:30 PT and reachable via Slack or phone.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Platform Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
